title: GS21 with TWO independent priced chains and two types, each with the PRODUCT exposure z~ b~ to one of them (K 1 -> 2 priced states beyond x), at gvyp10's exposure size and total price
question: Does a priced second factor make a fair gap in GS21 when the exposure is the PRODUCT of two within-firm states that two different characteristics reveal, so the premium is bilinear in the ranks?
notes: Campaign 2026-10-12, group 4 cell for GS21 (docs/CAMPAIGN_REPORT_2026-10-11). The control is gvyp10 (one 9-node chain, one type, gs_bv 0.1 on z~ b~, gamma_v 2.5). Here y2 is a second Tauchen chain, independent of y1, same kappa; the state is the joint node (5 x 5 = 25 nodes; 5 per chain, not 9, to keep each type's solve near four hours: the solve's cost is linear in the joint count), every per-y table and the priced mixture run on it, and the panel exports y2_stand beside y_stand so the fair linear benchmark sees both states. Two types, shares 1/2: type a loads 0.1 z~ b~ on y1 only, type b 0.1 z~ b~ on y2 only, so the cross-section of exposures is two-dimensional (vym3t3's construction). Total price of y-risk unchanged, ||gamma|| = 2.5 split as 2.5/sqrt(2) per chain. Validation: a low-resolution parity run (xnum 21, NY 3) with a dead second chain reproduces the single chain's tables; see the gate.

changes: gs_bv [0.1, 0.0] x gs_bzb 1.0 z~ b~: productivity x coupon exposure, single type
the y factor moves the COST, exp(gs_bc y), with types gs_bc [0.0, 0.0]; production exposure gs_bv 0, no level compensation (at y = 0 every type pays the same cost)
everything else gvy25's: 9-node priced y chain, gamma_v 2.5, kappa_y 0.35

method.gs_vy_exposure: production x exp(gs_bv gs_bzb z~ b~ y)

seeds.policy: run_oracle.py --seed drives BOTH the firm-level shocks and the aggregate y path (reg_seed offset by the seed).
